what_this_is: How an existing page's repeater rows become an ordered list of `blocks` rows.
Data, not code: Phase 3 adds routes here, it does not add PHP. cms/import/backfill-blocks.php
is the only reader, and everything it knows about a page is in this file.
Reviewable in a pull request BEFORE it runs, which is the point — the script writes one
field on one page and is undone by emptying that field in wp-admin, but it is still the
step that decides what the page is made of. docs/PAGE-BLOCKS.md 1.4.
the_rule_that_governs_every_value_below: A backfilled page must render markup IDENTICAL to the template band it replaces — class
names, element order, attributes. So a value here is only ever one of three things:
1. a row that already exists in the CMS, moved (never copied, never re-typed);
2. a value the template hardcodes TODAY, transcribed verbatim, with the source line
named in `from_template` so a reviewer can diff it against the file;
3. a layout switch (`band`, `columns`, `ratio`) read off the page's own stylesheet,
with the rule that proves it named in `band_evidence`.
Nothing here is authored. If a value is not in the CMS and not in the template, it does
not belong in this file — it is content the client has yet to write, and inventing it
here would change the page the moment the backfill ran.

source_kinds._: The closed set of sources a `fields` entry may name. The backfill rejects anything else.
source_kinds.{ \"section\": \"<name>\" }: A sub-field of the `sections` row this block is built from: eyebrow, heading, body, cta_label, cta_href.
source_kinds.{ \"literal\": <scalar> }: A fixed value. Pair it with `from_template` naming the line it was transcribed from.
source_kinds.{ \"toc_label\": true }: The `toc_links` row whose anchor equals this block's anchor. The default for nav_label.
source_kinds.{ \"image\": \"<slot>\", \"part\": \"id\: The attachment id in the `images` row with that slot.

row_kinds._: The closed set of sources a `rows` entry may name — these fill a repeater INSIDE a block.
row_kinds.{ \"literal\": [ … ] }: Rows given here in full. Same rule as above: transcription, not authoring.
row_kinds.{ \"cards\": \"<group>\", \"fields\": {: The `cards` rows in that group, in order. `fields` maps block sub-field <- card sub-field. `literal`, if present, is zipped onto them positionally and must be the same length — that is how a list whose text lives in the CMS but whose labels live in the template is reassembled without losing either.
row_kinds.{ \"process_steps\": true, \"fields\": {: Every `process_steps` row on the page, in order.
row_kinds.{ \"faqs\": true, \"fields\": { … } }: Every `faqs` row on the page, in order.
row_kinds.@index2: The one derivation allowed on the right-hand side of `fields`: the 1-based row number, zero-padded to two digits. It exists because the legacy `process_steps` repeater has no `num` sub-field — src/loaders/pages.ts:537 derives it as String(i+1).padStart(2,'0') and the page prints that. Anything else would renumber the steps.

defaults.anchor: the block's `section_id`, unless the block sets `anchor` explicitly. Carried across so existing #fragment links, the derived rail and every scroll-margin-top target keep pointing at the same element.
defaults.nav_label: { "toc_label": true } — blank when the page has no toc_links row for this anchor, which keeps the block out of the rail exactly as it is out of it today.

_: Layouts this map names that vs-content-model.php does not register. The backfill checks
every one before it plans anything and stops while any is missing, rather than writing
rows whose sub-fields ACF would drop without a word.
Not empty. Seven of the eight layouts the pilot needs are registered in the repository;
`code_section` is the eighth and is registered nowhere — not in vs-content-model.php, not
in src/blocks/manifest.ts, not in src/blocks/registry.ts. Phase 1 deferred it reasoning
that the pilot needed none of them; the pilot needs exactly one, and the page moved a band
while it was missing. See the `code_section` row in the route below.
Being registered in the repository is also not the same as being on the CMS host, which
is a separate check the backfill makes first — see the file header of backfill-blocks.php.

code_section.spec: docs/PAGE-BLOCKS.md 1.3, "The escape hatch — code_section". A layout with no editable content: it names a band that stays in code, and an editor can move it and delete it but cannot author it. That is the whole difference between "stays in code" and "cannot be positioned", and conflating the two is what put LocalTrust at the bottom of this page.

sub_fields.anchor: text. The band's DOM id. Carried, not generated: it is a public address — inbound links, the derived rail, and every scroll-margin-top target key off it.
sub_fields.nav_label: text. Filled by the backfill from the `toc_links` row whose anchor matches, exactly as it is for every other layout. This is what puts a code-owned band back in the rail.
sub_fields.band_key: select, readonly label, closed list. Names which bespoke band this row holds the place of. One choice is needed today: local_trust -> vivid-smiles-website/src/components/LocalTrust.astro.

code_section.no_preamble: No eyebrow/heading/body. src/blocks/manifest.ts:85-88 says so in as many words — code_section is `anchor navLabel band bandKey` and nothing else, and asking it for `heading` fails query validation for every page on the site rather than for this one.
code_section.no_containers: No repeaters and no groups, so assert_unique_block_container_names() (vs-content-model.php:366) has nothing to collide here. It is the one layout that cannot trip that check.

Four bands on this page draw one. `compare` and `process` draw theirs entirely from the

The fix is a second CTA pair on the layout in vs-content-model.php, and until it exists
this map gets the primary button right and the secondary is gone. Named in

THE LOCALTRUST BAND SITS BETWEEN `lasting` AND `gallery` AND IS NOW IN THIS LIST, at

while the template's <LocalTrust> stays at :494, so the band that belongs between `lasting`
and `gallery` came out after `faq`. Template order stopped being page order the moment the
blocks took over, and a band that is not in the list has no position in it.
Nothing about the band itself changes. It is still drawn by LocalTrust.astro with the props
clear-aligners.astro gives it, and it is still not editable. Only its POSITION moves into
the ordered list, which is what code_section is for — docs/PAGE-BLOCKS.md 1.3 and 1.4 step 5.

one_row_not_two: A CLASS-PREFIX READING OF THE BUILT HTML FINDS LOCAL-TRUST TWICE. There is one band.
The first hit is the scoped <style> Astro hoists into <head> for LocalTrust.astro —
`.vs-lt { ... }`, which on the built page precedes <body> — and a stylesheet is not a
band. It reads at position 1 both before and after the migration, which is the tell: the
band moved and that did not, because a rule in <head> has nowhere to move to. Anything
counting bands by class prefix has to skip <head>, or it will keep reporting this.
clear-aligners.astro imports LocalTrust once (:34) and invokes it once (:494), and the
built page carries exactly one id="local" and one <section class="vs-lt">. So this is ONE
row. A second one would put an empty LocalTrust band on the page, and PageBlocks would
rename its anchor to #local-2 (PageBlocks.astro:72-82) — breaking the rail entry and the
inbound links that this row exists to keep pointing at the same element.
blocks.nav_label_note: Resolves to "Parker, CO" from the `toc_links` row whose anchor is `local`, by the same default every other block uses. That is the row that used to sit under `exempt.toc_links`; claiming the anchor here is what brings the rail entry back, and it is why that list is now empty.
known_gaps: code_section is registered nowhere, so `pending_layouts` above is no longer empty and the
migration screen stops at preflight until vs-content-model.php registers it. That is a
deploy, and the contract it has to satisfy is written out in that entry.
vs_bb_plan_route() requires a `sections` row for every block — backfill-blocks.php:438-460
fails a block with no `section_id`, and then fails one whose `section_id` names no row. A
code_section has no row by definition, so the planner needs to let a block that names an
`anchor` and no `section_id` through with an empty section. Nothing else in the planner
needs to know: `fields` here asks for nothing from a section, and the toc_links claim is
already keyed on the anchor rather than on the section id (:476-479).
THE BAND'S COPY STAYS IN THE TEMPLATE, and band_key does not carry it. heading,
headingItalic, intro and body are hardcoded at clear-aligners.astro:494-499, so a renderer
that drew LocalTrust from band_key alone would print some other page's heading here — a
visible change, which is the one thing this file exists to prevent. Whoever writes the
code_section renderer keeps the invocation where it is and renders it at this row's
position. Moving that copy into the CMS is `map_visit`, Wave B, Phase 4, and that layout
REPLACES this row rather than joining it — two rows for one band is the #local-2 fault above.

literal.heading: What to Expect During Your Teeth Whitening Appointment
literal.body: A Vivid Smiles whitening appointment begins with a consultation to assess your staining type, confirm shade goals, and select the right KöR level. Dr. Richardson's team follows specific protocols to manage sensitivity so the experience stays comfortable from first application to finish.

literal.heading: In-Office vs At-Home KöR Whitening
literal.body: In-office KöR Power treatment combines three 20-minute chair sessions with custom take-home trays for ongoing maintenance. At-home KöR-Night uses custom trays worn nightly for two weeks, with results building gradually. Many patients combine both: in-office for the initial lift, then take-home trays for maintenance.

KöR professional whitening is safe for most healthy adults when supervised by a trained dental provider.

KöR formulations are developed to protect enamel while maximizing whitening efficacy, unlike the unregulated products sold online or in salons. Dr. Richardson assesses enamel condition and gum health before treatment begins, and KöR's gel chemistry is specifically engineered to reduce post-treatment sensitivity compared to older whitening formulas. Professional oversight is what separates safe, lasting results from unpredictable outcomes.

The key `teeth_whitening_local` is now registered on both sides: as a choice
in BLOCK_CODE_BANDS (cms/mu-plugins/vs-content-model.php) and as an entry in

LocalTrust on both pages, but its copy is page content, so a shared key would
put 'for Clear Aligners' on the whitening page.
Adding a page therefore means adding BOTH — a choice and a BANDS entry, in
the same commit. Miss either and the row writes cleanly and renders nothing.

known_gaps: 1. THE PORTRAIT PLATE BECOMES LANDSCAPE, AND THIS IS THE LARGEST GAP ON THE ROUTE.
all-on-4-single-arch.css:308-311 gives `.what-img`, `.robotics-img` and `.natural-img`
a shared `aspect-ratio: 4/5`, and :316 overrides only `.what-img` back to 5/4. So
`.robotics-img` is a PORTRAIT plate, and roboticsImg is a portrait file — 1152x1365,
confirmed live. MediaSplitBlock ties the frame to the side (`.what-img` 5/4,
`.natural-img` 4/5) on the measured claim in its own header that no page mixes the two.
This band mixes them, so `media_side: left` puts a 1152x1365 source into a 5/4 frame
with `object-fit: cover` and crops roughly a third of its height.
THE TRADE, STATED SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT RE-LITIGATE IT: `media_side: right` would
give the correct 4/5 frame and move the photograph to the other side of the page,
reversing the reading order of a band whose copy runs heading -> prose -> callout down
the right-hand column. Reading order and column proportions are kept; the crop is lost.
WHAT CLOSES IT: a `media_shape` select on the layout — `landscape` | `portrait`,
defaulting to whatever the side already implies — read by MediaSplitBlock as a
`.what-img.portrait` / `.natural-img.landscape` modifier. The frame stops being a
consequence of the side. Two scoped rules and one select; no new component.
2. THE CLASS FAMILY. The band comes back as `.what-grid.ratio-wide-media` >
`.what-img` + `.what-text`, where the template ships `.robotics-grid` >
`.robotics-img` + `.robotics-text`. The page sheet styles `.robotics-*` at

media_side_decision: READ OFF THE RULE, NOT OFF THE CLASS NAME. The band is
<div class="natural-grid alt-flip"> (gum-contouring.astro:466) and `.alt-flip` is this
page's own modifier: gum-contouring.css:541-546 sets grid-template-columns 1.1fr 1fr,
`.natural-img { order: 0 }` and `.natural-text { order: 1 }`. So the PHOTO IS ON THE LEFT
and the photo's column is the wider one. `media_side` is a fact about the band, and the
fact is `left`.
`ratio` follows from the same rule. MediaSplitBlock writes its tracks photo-relative, so
the 1.1fr-photo / 1fr-text split IS `wide-media`; on the left-photo family that is not the
default, so `.what-grid.ratio-wide-media` (MediaSplitBlock.astro:781-783) is emitted and
reproduces the alt-flip column widths exactly.
WHAT THIS COSTS is in known_gaps below: media_side also selects the class FAMILY
(MediaSplitBlock.astro:276 — `const fam = mediaRight ? "natural" : "what"`), so `left`
brings the `.what-*` names and the 5/4 plate with it.
`right` WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. It keeps `.natural-grid`, `.natural-img` and the 4/5
plate, and loses instead the thing the band exists for: the template's own comment at
:463-465 says alt-flip is there so "the image lands on the left and the text on the
right, giving the page rhythm a different shape from the Laser section above". `right`
would mirror the band and put a second right-hand photo under the first. One value keeps
the composition and changes the crop; the other keeps the crop and destroys the
composition. The composition is what the page was designed around, so: left.
blocks.prose_note: TWO paragraphs in .prose (gum-contouring.astro:477-486) and both are carried — `body` from the CMS row, `body_2` above. No quote on this band (that is `laser`'s), no callout aside and no CTA row, so none of those fields is supplied.
known_gaps: THE PHOTO PLATE CHANGES SHAPE, FROM A 4/5 PORTRAIT TO A 5/4 LANDSCAPE. THIS IS THE
LARGEST LOSS ON THIS ROUTE.
media_split has two class families and `media_side` selects both the side and the family
(MediaSplitBlock.astro:276). `left` is the `.what-*` family, so the backfilled band comes
back as:
<div class="what-grid ratio-wide-media"> <div class="what-img">…  <div class="what-text">…
where the template ships
<div class="natural-grid alt-flip"> <div class="natural-img">…  <div class="natural-text">…
DOM order is identical and the column split is identical (1.1fr photo / 1fr text, from
`.what-grid.ratio-wide-media` at MediaSplitBlock.astro:781-783 against
`.natural-grid.alt-flip` at gum-contouring.css:541-546). What differs is the plate:
`.what-img` is aspect-ratio 5/4 (MediaSplitBlock.astro:795) and `.natural-img` is 4/5
(:813). resultsImg is 1000x1250 — a portrait — so object-fit: cover in a 5/4 box shows a
1000x800 centre crop of a 1250-tall frame and drops roughly 18% off the top and the bottom
of a patient portrait. That is a content change, not a styling one, and it is why this is
written up as the route's largest gap rather than as a class-name difference.
The three class names also stop matching the page sheet, so the rules at
gum-contouring.css:541-546 go unused while the band renders. They are LEFT IN PLACE: the
else branch is the rollback path and needs every one of them.
WHAT CLOSES IT: MediaSplitBlock emitting the natural family with the media first — that
is the `.natural-grid.alt-flip` shape, which no page-agnostic rule currently produces. It
needs a third choice on the `media_side` select in cms/mu-plugins/vs-content-model.php
(the family and the side stop being one axis), the matching branch in MediaSplitBlock
around `fam` and the two photo blocks, and the `.natural-grid.alt-flip` rules moved into
the component's own <style>. Additive to every saved row: `left` and `right` keep meaning
what they mean today. NOT DONE HERE — this route does not add fields or invent layouts,
and gum-contouring is the only page in src/pages that carries `.alt-flip` today.
Nothing else on this band is lost: eyebrow, heading, both prose paragraphs and the photo
itself are all carried.

on this band that costs money rather than pixels, and it is the error the veneers
entry avoided from the other direction by NOT supplying a qualifier its page does
not have.

ratio_is_even_on_purpose: the layout offers is `wide-text`, which is `1fr 1.1fr` — but the page sheet's own
(0,2,0), the SAME specificity as the block's `.what-grid.ratio-wide-text`, and file
order between a page stylesheet and a component's scoped styles is not guaranteed. So
`wide-text` would render 1fr 1.1fr or 1fr 1fr depending on link order.
`even` is chosen instead because it emits no modifier at all and both sheets then agree
on 1fr 1fr. A deterministic 1fr 1fr is worth more than a marginally closer value that
two stylesheets are racing for — and the difference from 0.9fr 1.1fr is named as a gap
below rather than hidden inside a cascade.

aspect field — it is `media_side: right`, which selects `.natural-*` and gives a 4/5

photo on the right, inverting the band's DOM order and its visual composition. Which
of the two is the smaller loss is a design call, and it is recorded here rather than

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the same treatment #technology's list gets — an additive alias in
sinus-lift.css giving `.sinuslift .compare` and `.sinuslift .compare-card` this page's
three values, deleting nothing, so `.alt-*` stays for the else branch. It is NOT done
here, and the difference between the two cases is worth stating: `.tech-list` and
`.candidate-list` are the same declarations character for character in all four sheets
that carry them, so an alias there cannot change a rendered pixel. These three values
differ, so an alias here would override the block's own geometry from a page sheet and
make this one band render unlike every other comparison_cards band on the site. That
is a design decision about which of the two shapes is correct, and it belongs to
whoever owns the design system, not to a migration.

notes: EIGHT BLOCKS, EIGHT SECTIONS ROWS, EIGHT TOC_LINKS ROWS, ONE ANCHOR APIECE. The page's
eight content bands — what, issues, process, options, why-us, cost, results, faq — are
the `sections` repeater's eight rows in the template's own order, and the eight

file header called #issues, #why-us and #results "cream" and #process "sage". Neither is

known_gaps: THE ★★★★★ RUN ON STAT CARD 1 CANNOT SURVIVE THE ROUND TRIP TODAY, and the fault is a type
disagreement between the layout and its component, not this map.
vs-content-model.php:3794-3800 declares copy_plus_stats' `stats.stars` as a true_false, so
ACF stores 1/0 and wpgraphql-acf exposes a Boolean. CopyPlusStatsBlock.astro:130 types it
`string | null`, funnels it through `text()` (:187-188, `typeof input === "string" ? … : ""`)
and prints the VALUE inside the span (:333). A Boolean therefore trims to "" and the whole
<span class="stars"> — plus its plain space and its   — draws nothing.
MediaSplitBlock, which the manifest cites as the same contract, gets this right: it types
`creds[].stars` as boolean, tests `row?.stars === true` (:653) and writes the five glyphs as
a literal in its own markup (:822). CopyPlusStatsBlock is the odd one out.
The glyphs are recorded above so nothing is lost from the map, and the value is what a
true_false coerces from anyway (any non-empty string stores as 1). The fix is one line in
CopyPlusStatsBlock — treat `stars` as truthy and emit the literal ★★★★★ — and it belongs to
whoever owns that component, not here. REPORTED, not fixed: three sibling agents are relying
on these components being stable.

solutions, compare, process, technology, doctors, candidacy, area, faq — and every one of
them is a block's anchor above, `area`'s included (the code_section claims it on the

notes: THREE OF FIVE CONTENT BANDS MOVE. This page's five bands are #cosmetic, #implants,
#everyday, #process and #faq, and its `sections` repeater holds exactly those five rows
in that order. Only the first three are here. #process and #faq stay TEMPLATE bands and
are exempted below, with the reasons written out there.
WHY THAT IS SAFE AND WHY IT IS A TAIL, NOT A GAP. An unguarded band renders where it sits
in the .astro file, which is after the whole block run — so leaving bands behind only
preserves page order while the ones left behind are a contiguous tail. #process is band 4
and #faq is band 5, so holding BOTH keeps the order exactly as it is today. Migrating #faq
on its own would lift it above #process and move a live band, which is the same mistake
that put LocalTrust below #faq on /cosmetic-dentistry/clear-aligners/ (see that route's
notes). #faq moves in the change that closes #process, not before it.
NO RAIL ON THIS ROUTE. /services/ has no `.toc` nav and pageFields.tocLinks is null on the
live endpoint, so nav_label resolves blank on all three blocks (the map's own default) and
the page carries no derivedTocLinks loop. Nothing to lose and nothing to keep in step.

--vs-charcoal-green) and `.section.dark` is the PALE one (:153-156 -> --vs-sage-pale).
